prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate objective function for a GNN-based netlist tier-partitioner (2-tier 3D IC).
Hypothesis of the change: Removing the criticality-weighted cut (`net_w`) and the macro-balance term from the parent restores the baseline backbone (which had the lowest crit_cross) while replacing the quadratic area balance with a silent-inside-deadband hinge plus a small linear pull, so the raw partition lands near 50% with fewer repair flips without perturbing the cut term that actually contains critical logic.
Rule-based digest (scores are improvement ratios vs. the official baseline; C1..C3 are the training circuits by size):
total=-0.514 robust(mean-std)=-0.280 min_case=-0.322 seed_std=0.345 tns_mean=-0.128 all_valid=True
  C1: score=-0.120 dWNS=-13.6% dTNS=-6.2% per-seed=[+0.06 -0.61 +0.19]
  C2: score=-0.322 dWNS=-32.2% dTNS=-30.5% per-seed=[+0.03 -0.51 -0.49]
  C3: score=-0.072 dWNS=-12.5% dTNS=+2.1% per-seed=[+0.45 -0.04 -0.63]
  partition stats vs baseline:
  C1: cut 137->129, wcut 421->406, crit_cross 0.011->0.115, repair_flips 103->77, changed-vs-baseline 21.9%
  C2: cut 318->339, wcut 1007->1141, crit_cross 0.000->0.128, repair_flips 238->201, changed-vs-baseline 33.7%
  C3: cut 582->551, wcut 1955->1840, crit_cross 0.069->0.080, repair_flips 353->264, changed-vs-baseline 32.6%
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID, first classify the failure (crash / non-finite loss / balance repair failure / timeout) and whether it is systematic or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which circuit/metric moved and the plausible mechanism (cut nets, critical-pair cross-tier, repair flips)? (3) is the seed spread acceptable? (4) one concrete next step. No preamble.

response: Hypothesis failed: removing `net_w` raised crit_cross sharply (C1 0.011→0.115, C2 0.000→0.128, C3 0.069→0.080) despite fewer repair flips (103→77, 238→201, 353→264) and modest cut/wcut changes. All scores negative (total −0.514), so the silent-deadband balance did not offset lost criticality weighting. Seed spread is unacceptable (seed_std 0.345; C3 per-seed +0.45 to −0.63). Next step: reinstate a light criticality-weighted cut term (small λ) while keeping the deadband hinge, and re-sweep λ on C2 to recover crit_cross without losing flip savings.
